newsitem.title: UK: BA gives British Mediterranean franchise.
newsitem.headline: BA gives British Mediterranean franchise.

text.p: British Airways Plc said it has agreed to team up with privately-owned British Mediterranean Airways (BMA) so that BMA will operate flights under a BA franchise to Lebanon, Jordan and Syria.
BA said that, from October 26, it will withdraw services to Beirut, Amman and Damascus.

Robert Ayling, BA chief executive said: "The restriction on the number of flights we can operate to Beirut means it is impossible for BA itself to serve this market and make an acceptable financial return."
"The franchise agreement...will ensure a British airline is able to mount viably competitive services on these routes."

BMA will then take over the flights from October 27 and will extend the network to Alexandria from December, with further expansion to Tblisi in Georgia, Bishkek in Kyrgystan and Tashkent in Uzebekistan planned for summer 1996, BA added in a statement.
No equity investment is involved and BMA will remain a separate independent company. It also appointed BA as its sales agent worldwide from October 27, the statement said.
However, BMA's aircraft will be repainted in BA livery, with cabin and customer staff wearing BA uniforms.

A BMA spokeswoman said the carrier now operates an Airbus Industrie A-320 on the route and the intention is to acquire an additional Airbus around November, with a further aircraft expected next spring as routes expand.
BMA was launched with a five-times-a-week flight to Beirut in October 1994 and this was expanded to include Damascus and Amman.
BA said it was only able to operate twice weekly services to Beirut and Damascus since resuming services there in early 1995.

"This made it impossible for BA to operate profitablity and with the same aircraft also used to serve Amman it has undermined the commercial viability of these flights too," it added. The Boeing 767 aircraft and crew will deployed to expand operations on more profitable services, including a seventh weekly flight to Kuwait and a third weekly frequency to Tehran, BA said.
